holidays.name: National Rum Day
holidays.description: A day for raising a glass to the molasses-based spirit of pirates and tiki bars. Fans sip classic daiquiris, mojitos, and dark-and-stormies, or just pour a little over some pineapple.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance with no single documented founder. It grew in popularity through social media and spirits marketing, and is separate from International Rum Day, which is celebrated on other dates by some groups.
holidays.funFact: Rum was once part of the daily ration for sailors in the British Royal Navy, a tradition that lasted until 1970 and was known as the 'Tot'.

holidays.name: National Roller Coaster Day
holidays.description: A thrill-seeker's holiday for screaming, laughing, and clutching the safety bar as you plummet down a hill at high speed. Amusement park fans celebrate by riding their favorite coasters.
holidays.origin: Celebrated on August 16 because it marks the anniversary of the patent for the first American roller coaster, the 'Switchback Railway', granted to LaMarcus Adna Thompson in 1885.
holidays.funFact: The Switchback Railway at Coney Island opened in 1884 and only reached about 6 miles per hour, yet people lined up to pay a nickel to ride it.

holidays.name: National Tell a Joke Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to groaning at puns, delivering punchlines, and annoying your coworkers with dad jokes. The worse the joke, the better the celebration.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that popped up in humor circles and on calendars of fun days, encouraging people to share laughter with friends, family, and strangers.
holidays.funFact: One of the oldest known recorded jokes is a Sumerian proverb about a husband and wife, dating back to around 1900 BC.

holidays.name: National Bratwurst Day
holidays.description: A salute to the German sausage that sizzles on grills, nestles in buns, and begs for a generous squirt of mustard and a pile of sauerkraut.
holidays.origin: This food holiday is celebrated in the United States on August 16, with the day promoted by sausage fans and food calendars as a nod to German culinary heritage, particularly popular in Wisconsin.
holidays.funFact: The word 'bratwurst' comes from Old High German 'brät' meaning finely chopped meat, and 'wurst' meaning sausage. It does not come from the word 'braten' (to fry), though many people assume it does.

holidays.name: Bennington Battle Day
holidays.description: A Vermont state holiday remembering a Revolutionary War victory, celebrated with parades, reenactments, and plenty of local pride.
holidays.origin: It commemorates the Battle of Bennington on August 16, 1777, when American forces defeated a detachment of British and German troops that had gone looking for supplies, including horses and, reportedly, food.
holidays.funFact: Although the battle is named after Bennington, Vermont, it was actually fought in Walloomsac, New York, a few miles away.
